definition: The strange wistfulness of used bookshops, that ache felt when confronted with so many lives and worlds that one will never have time to read — a sense of time folded densely upon itself.
etymology: Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows (2013), built from Latin volumen, a rolled manuscript, and ichor, the ethereal fluid that runs in the veins of the gods in Greek myth. Koenig fused the bookish and the divine to name a feeling that had no name, which is itself a very bookish act.
usage: She lingered in the cramped back aisle until vellichor overtook her — every cracked spine a door she would never open, every margin note a stranger's whispered confidence lost to time.
